_comment: Live config. Both Gemini Pro-tier options are dead ends: gemini-3.1-pro-preview hit a hard 429 quota-exceeded (needs billing enabled, not just a low free allowance) and gemini-2.5-pro came back 404 'no longer available to new users' - a real decommission, not a rate issue. A role's value can be a single {provider, model, ...} dict, or a LIST of them - a fallback chain tried in preference order, falling back only once a candidate's own internal retries are fully exhausted (see providers.call_model/_dispatch). 2026-09-20, three changes the same night, in order: (1) swapped action/character/atmosphere/unify off gemini-3.6-flash onto gemini-3.5-flash-lite, moved editor the other way (3.5-flash-lite -> 3.6-flash), after three straight days of 503 'high demand' storms outlasting the full retry backoff - the run that nailed it down failed on action, the very FIRST call of a fresh regeneration, proving it's the model under sustained load, not any one pass's payload. Flash-lite is Google's own high-throughput tier (lower per-call intelligence, built for exactly this kind of volume) vs 3.6-flash's heavier 'workhorse' tier - editor, the one role on 3.6-flash that night, had not 503'd once in two weeks, versus every role on 3.6-flash 503ing repeatedly. (2) Every role turned into an explicit fallback chain, at the user's direct request to hedge against a whole provider having a bad night, not just one model: action/character/atmosphere/unify chain lite -> 3.6-flash -> Groq gpt-oss-120b -> Mistral -> Cerebras; editor chains 3.6-flash -> Groq -> Mistral -> Cerebras, deliberately never listing flash-lite so it can't coincidentally land on unify's exact model that call; skeleton and summariser keep their proven Groq model first (skeleton's input never includes the motif section and has held up across every chapter; summariser doesn't send canon.md, so its input stays small) with Gemini/Mistral/Cerebras behind it as extra insurance neither had shown a need for yet. Mistral and Cerebras were both parked earlier in the project (Mistral: 429 rate_limited on the very first call, two different roles, two separate runs; Cerebras: the specific model tried then, llama-4-maverick-17b-128e-instruct, was archived) - as the LAST resort in a chain they cost nothing to list again: if they still don't work the chain just falls through to a real error same as before they existed, and if they've recovered since, that's a free extra layer. Picked mistral-small-latest deliberately (a '-latest' alias, not a dated snapshot) to dodge the exact version-churn that broke qwen3.6-27b and gemini-3.1-pro-preview elsewhere in this file; Cerebras's llama3.3-70b is a different, currently-supported model from the archived one. (3) run_chapter.py now also caps how many fresh prose passes ONE run attempts (MAX_NEW_PASSES_PER_RUN, default 2) before stopping cleanly (exit 0) and leaving the rest for the next scheduled fire - a second, independent line of defense bounding a single run's blast radius regardless of which failure mode causes it, on top of (not instead of) the fallback chains. summariser also carries reasoning_effort/reasoning_format on its Groq candidate - its original model (qwen/qwen3.6-27b) was a reasoning model that emitted <think>...</think> as literal text sharing the same token budget as the real answer, burning through 500 then 2000 tokens on chapter 2 without ever finishing its reasoning, let alone writing the summary. These fields (read by providers._openai_compatible, ignored by roles/candidates that don't set them) disable reasoning outright and strip it from the response as a second line of defense. qwen/qwen3.6-27b itself was then decommissioned outright (404 model_not_found) - moved summariser's primary to openai/gpt-oss-20b, the smaller sibling of skeleton's gpt-oss-120b: same family, distinct model ID so no shared TPM concerns, small enough for a task that never sends canon.md anyway. Two live 400s fixing that: qwen accepted reasoning_effort 'none' but gpt-oss only accepts low/medium/high (set to 'low'), and reasoning_format isn't supported by gpt-oss at all - had to drop it. Not a problem in practice: gpt-oss puts reasoning in its own response field rather than qwen's literal inline tags, so the content field _openai_compatible() reads was never going to carry reasoning text regardless. _strip_thinking() in passes.py stays as a no-cost safety net for whatever model ends up on this role next.
